copy_pick.why: Its headline 'MISSILES FALL ON THE AID LINE' best fits the wire-service deadpan with one verb and no adjectives, and its summary stays tight, specific and witty ('the war hasn't been told yet') without recycling stale items like Candidate 3's Binance heist or its two-verb headline.

doom.driver: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing. Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.
doom.blurb: MISSILES FALL ON THE AID LINE
doom.summary: While America spent the night refreshing electoral maps, Moscow timed 365 drones and missiles to the returns and hit an aid site, leaving 29 dead and 48 missing. Tehran's speaker cheered the 'NO TO WAR' vote, but the war hasn't been told yet. Meanwhile, OpenAI quietly re-ticked your data-sharing box, and a bootkit learned to walk straight past Secure Boot.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: A 27B model reading weights on a laptop and Siri taking the controls of every app add up to a real step forward.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Voters restored the checks and balances, while the DOJ sent target letters and Google held school search hostage to Gemini.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Russia's election-night barrage killed 29 people at an aid site as the US-Iran conflict hovers near a new escalation.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Opt-outs quietly turning back into opt-ins at OpenAI and Postman show that consent is still treated as a default setting.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Bomb threats on seven European flights and a disputed shell in Papua New Guinea are worrying but not spreading.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A wide aerial view looking down at a 45-degree angle over the flat black steppe of Zaporizhzhia Oblast at night, a vast ploughed field stretching to a horizon swallowed by smoke, with a thin line of bare windbreak trees and a ribbon of wet dirt road cutting across it. A hellish deep-red glow rises from below the frame and from cracks in the earth, lighting the underside of low smoke clouds in crimson against near-black. The central visual metaphor is a giant chessboard laid into the field, its squares formed by the furrows and frost-whitened patches. The board is mid-collapse: the near half has split and subsided into a glowing red crater, and the squares tilt and slide into it. Scattered across the board stand oversized chess pieces, mostly black pawns, a few toppled. One dark pawn rests at the crater's very lip, leaning over the edge. At the far side, a single lone white king stands untouched, small and pale against the darkness. Along the road, a few tiny rescuers in reflective-striped gear, each shown whole, stand in a loose line near the crater with a single stretcher, dwarfed by the scale. Embers drift upward in the red-black air. Extreme contrast, suffocating darkness, palette limited to deep crimson, blood red, ember orange touches, and black.

minor: The scene is extremely dark. The rescuers and stretcher the prompt asked for can't be made out, and the toppled pawns are barely visible.
The crater reads as a pit of tilted dark diamond tiles, and its geometry is confusing. It is hard to tell which parts are board squares and which are debris.
A wood-grain diagonal band in the lower right, presumably the wet dirt road, looks more like a plank or beam than a road.
The lone white king on the far side is small and dim, and it reads more like a pale bishop or pawn silhouette.
Dark pawn silhouettes on the board are mostly lost in shadow, and the one at the crater lip is hard to distinguish.

dawn.driver: A 50-year-old mystery of vanishing frogs reveals a hidden killer. A nearly 50-year-old mystery involving disappearing frogs in Brazil may finally be solved, with scientists uncovering evidence that a deadly fungus swept through the region and devastated vulnerable species. Remarkably, many frog populations have since rebounded, suggesting they developed greater tolerance to the disease
dawn.summary: Many of Brazil's frogs have come back. Scientists solving a half-century-old puzzle found that numerous populations recovered after a fungus swept through, apparently growing tougher against it, a reminder of how resourceful nature can be when given time. Out in space, samples from the asteroid Ryugu turned out to hold all five genetic letters of DNA and RNA, and Voyager 1 is nearly one full light-day from home, still sending word back nearly 50 years after launch.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Researchers found all five nucleobases of DNA and RNA in pristine samples from the 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid Ryugu, adding to the evidence that life's building blocks were widespread in the early solar system.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Brazil published the first global roadmap for phasing out coal, oil and gas, giving every country practical steps it can start on now.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Voters elected the nation's first Black woman governor and its first Native American woman governor, widening who gets to lead.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Frog populations in Brazil have rebounded and appear to have built tolerance to a fungus that once overwhelmed them.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Voyager 1 is about to become the first human-made object one light-day from Earth, its mission extended by a clever energy-saving maneuver.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 3 is the freshest: it avoids the 'Farther out'/'Further out' transitions recycled from the Oct 29 and Oct 17 cards, keeps a quiet nature-documentary headline in the directive's form, and accurately says 'many' frogs came back rather than overclaiming.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. WEATHER-DOMINATED scene of a smallholder's backyard on the forested edge of a small village in the Serra do Mar foothills, São Paulo state, Brazil, at first light. This is an adjacent place, far below the research station, where the returning frogs are heard rather than studied. Thick warm amber-gold mist pours down the green mountainside and fills the whole frame. Everything beyond the near foreground softens into layered silhouettes of tree ferns, banana plants and distant forested ridges, in soft green and honey-amber tones. Clean morning light brightens the haze from behind, so the shadows lift and the air clears toward the lower left. Elements: (1) a small rain-fed garden pond with a mossy stone rim, its surface scattered with lily pads and ringed by dewy grass. About seven small, healthy, generic Atlantic Forest tree frogs and pond frogs sit on the pads and stones in the foreground, glossy and alert. Several have their vocal sacs puffed out mid-chorus, and tiny ripples spread from them. (2) A bromeliad-covered wooden fence post beside the pond, with beads of water on the leaves and one bright green frog tucked into a leaf cup. (3) A modest whitewashed farmhouse with an orange clay-tile roof, half-dissolved in the mist in the middle distance, with a single warm amber lit doorway. (4) An old woman in a pale shawl, drawn whole and small, standing on the stone path with a steaming enamel mug. She is listening to the frog chorus with her head tilted toward the pond. (5) Banana leaves in the foreground, heavy with droplets, framing the scene on the right, with soft shafts of golden light cutting through the fog above the pond. The mood is quiet, reverent and gently triumphant, as if the forest's voice has come back.

minor: The old woman at right is small and partly overlapped by banana leaves and foliage, so her mug and hands read a little ambiguously, but her body is complete and connected.
A few frogs, especially the lower-center ones, have slightly blobby limbs that merge into the lily pads, which is acceptable at pixel-art scale.
The bromeliad frog is tucked into the leaf cup and is small and hard to read, but it is recognizable as a frog.
The farmhouse roofline and the lean-to roof on the left are slightly muddled in the haze, which suits the mist.
